postgres_requirements.rationale: T15 requires the Real-PG critical suite, the 42883 / 25P02 / new-transaction recovery semantics and the text[] real-driver coverage to be re-observed green at the synchronized head. None of those is answerable by a mock: 42883 and 25P02 are SQLSTATEs a real server emits, and text[] parameter binding is a real-driver behaviour -- it is MEASURED in this repository that drizzle's sql template EXPANDS a JS array into a parameter list rather than binding text[], so a mocked driver would agree with a broken implementation. Always via pnpm db:audit:disposable against a fresh throwaway container, destroyed afterwards; never staging, never production, never the canonical local Supabase stack. Both manifest paths are UNKNOWN because they remain pre-implementation commitments and the retry lane will author them at its own base. TWO MEASURED SUBSTRATE HAZARDS, carried forward so the retry lane does not rediscover them: (1) on supabase/postgres:17.6.1.143 the postgres role is NOT a superuser and cannot create the uellix_stella_ops schema -- take the proof as supabase_admin, and assert SETUP=SUCCESS explicitly rather than inferring setup health from probe colour; (2) the Real-PG suites must be run SERIALLY -- concurrent execution produces a non-zero process exit from afterAll leftovers even when every test passes, which would present a green suite as a failed gate.

Both are driven at the lane's OWN synchronized head. Required assertions: the RED is attributed to at least one NAMED inherited path that the mutant admits and the immutable form excludes -- never to a bare non-zero failure count, because a bare count cannot distinguish the mutation from a crash; and the witness path is RE-DERIVED at the lane's own base. Catches T12 and N-RC-15.

M2 -- the exact-write-set control still closes. Inject one 14th path into the immutable certified slice measurement and prove the exact-write-set control turns RED. Required assertions: the RED NAMES the injected 14th path; and the injected path is one that is NOT protected and NOT a FIBIU-19 path, so that the RED is attributable to the closed-enumeration control alone and cannot be double-counted against N-RC-08 or N-RC-05. This separation is the point of the mutant: three controls can all redden on one bad input, and a battery that does not isolate them proves only that something failed. Catches T12 and N-RC-12.

M3 -- N-RC-08 still refuses protected paths. Substitute a protected path into the certified slice measurement and prove N-RC-08 turns RED. TWO arms are required because the certified control refuses through two structurally different assertions and a single mutant would leave one unproven: MUT-RC-16-A substitutes a path under a db/** protected prefix, which is caught by the protectedPrefixes loop; MUT-RC-16-B substitutes a path under docs/ops/ods/, which is caught by the separate trailing assertion -- and this is the arm that reproduces the ACTUAL post-sync contradiction, since the inherited ODS maintenance addendum is what reddened N-RC-08 at 4680ae9c. A third arm SHOULD substitute a non-canonically-cased variant, since the certified control lower-cases both sides precisely to catch that and the arm is otherwise unproven. Each arm must assert RED with the offending path NAMED. Catches N-RC-12.

M4 -- N-RC-05 still refuses FIBIU-19 paths. Substitute a FIBIU-19 path into the certified slice measurement and prove N-RC-05 turns RED. The mutant MUST use lib/pipeline/sroi-results.ts specifically. That path is chokepoint SW-6 and the domain authority's own stated reason for serialising FIBIU-19 before FIBIU-20; the owner's sequencing exception (RC-02) is conditional on the slice not touching it, so a mutant exercising a lesser FIBIU-19 path would leave the load-bearing one unproven and the exception's condition uncontrolled. A second arm SHOULD exercise the directory-prefix form app/app/projects/[projectId]/pipeline/calculation/, because N-RC-05 matches by both equality and startsWith and the prefix branch is otherwise unproven. Catches N-RC-12.

The present-tense untracked arm is not vacuous. Introduce an untracked path outside the single-file authorized surface and prove N-RC-14 turns RED. This mutant exists because N-RC-14 asserts an EMPTINESS over a working tree that is clean in CI, and an emptiness assertion that is never driven non-empty is green forever and proves nothing -- it would be an arm retained in name only, which is worse than a deleted arm because it reads as protection. Required assertions: the RED NAMES the introduced untracked path; the introduced path is removed by the harness afterwards; and the control asserts SETUP=SUCCESS, so a harness that failed to create the file cannot present its own failure as a passing emptiness check. Catches N-RC-14.
